title: Fail-Safe Frames: Why Chips&Media’s ASIL-B Video IP Matters - Semiwiki
gist: Chips&Media's WAVE6331X FuSa video codec IP earned ISO 26262 ASIL-B automotive functional-safety certification from DNV after over two years of development, adding real-time fault detection across multiple codecs (H.264, HEVC, AV1, VP9) while minimizing added silicon area and power, positioning the company -- already used by three of the top five automotive semiconductor firms -- to compete on safety trust rather than just codec performance.

themes.theme: Why video processing is becoming safety-critical

insights.claim: As vehicles evolve into software-defined, increasingly autonomous platforms, video processing from camera feeds supporting surround-view monitoring, driver assistance, object detection and automated driving is becoming part of the safety-critical computing chain, since corrupted, delayed, or frozen frames can cause a vehicle to make decisions using incomplete or inaccurate visual information.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: This reframes video codec IP, historically a consumer multimedia commodity, as a safety-critical automotive component subject to the same certification rigor as braking or steering systems.
insights.quote: A vehicle may make decisions using incomplete or inaccurate visual information.

insights.claim: Chips&Media's WAVE6331X FuSa video codec IP achieved ISO 26262 ASIL-B certification from independent certification body DNV following more than two years of research and development, marking the company's expansion from consumer multimedia technology into safety-conscious automotive semiconductor applications.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: A multi-year, third-party-audited safety certification is a meaningful barrier to entry that differentiates Chips&Media from consumer-focused codec IP vendors without automotive-grade credentials.

insights.claim: ISO 26262 Automotive Safety Integrity Levels (ASILs) range from ASIL-A through ASIL-D, and achieving ASIL-B requires a structured safety lifecycle, documented engineering processes, systematic verification, and mechanisms for identifying and controlling relevant faults -- more than meeting a conventional performance specification.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Understanding where ASIL-B sits on the A-to-D scale helps investors and OEMs calibrate how much safety rigor this IP represents versus higher-stakes ASIL-D components like braking or steering.
insights.locator: ISO 26262 provides a framework for managing risks

themes.theme: Technical safety mechanisms and design tradeoffs

insights.claim: WAVE6331X FuSa detects internal hardware faults and data corruption during vehicle operation in real time using cyclic redundancy check (CRC) protection and instruction-flow monitoring, and can notify the wider system and support a transition to a safe state within a defined fault-response interval.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Real-time fault detection with a bounded response interval is the concrete mechanism that could prevent a frozen or corrupted video frame from propagating into a bad driving decision.
insights.locator: WAVE6331X FuSa is designed to detect internal hardware faults

insights.claim: Functional-safety mechanisms typically require redundant logic, monitoring circuitry and diagnostic functions that increase silicon area and power consumption, a real tradeoff in automotive systems where thermal limits, energy efficiency and cost all matter; Chips&Media says its low-power architecture integrates the necessary safety measures while minimizing that overhead.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: If verified independently, minimizing the area/power penalty of functional safety would be a genuine competitive advantage over rival automotive codec IP that trades off more silicon for the same certification level.
insights.locator: The architecture also addresses a persistent engineering tradeoff

insights.claim: Chips&Media extended its ISO 26262-based functional-safety development approach across AVC/H.264, HEVC/H.265, AV1 and VP9, giving semiconductor manufacturers freedom to select codecs based on compression efficiency, bandwidth, and image quality without abandoning a structured functional-safety strategy.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Multi-codec safety coverage removes a common lock-in constraint where automotive designers previously stuck with older codecs specifically to avoid re-certification cost, broadening Chips&Media's addressable design wins.
insights.locator: Another important aspect is codec flexibility

insights.claim: WAVE6331X FuSa is certified as a Safety Element out of Context (SEooC), meaning it was developed against defined assumptions before integration into a particular vehicle system; customers must still validate the complete system, but the certified SEooC package -- including safety manuals and development guidance -- can reduce duplicated analysis and shorten integration and assessment work for automotive SoC developers and Tier 1 suppliers.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: A pre-certified SEooC package shortens time-to-certification for OEM and Tier 1 customers, a concrete commercial selling point that can speed design-win cycles versus uncertified IP.
insights.locator: WAVE6331X FuSa is certified as a Safety Element out of Context

insights.claim: Chips&Media reports that its multimedia IP is already used by three of the world's five largest automotive semiconductor companies, giving the newly certified safety framework an existing distribution base to build on.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Pre-existing design-in relationships with three of the top five automotive semiconductor firms mean the ASIL-B certification can likely be cross-sold into an installed customer base rather than requiring new customer acquisition.
insights.locator: Commercially, the certification strengthens Chips&Media's position

insights.claim: Chips&Media plans to apply the same functional-safety framework to emerging AV2 and VVC compression technologies.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Extending safety certification to next-generation codecs (AV2, VVC) ahead of their broader industry adoption could let Chips&Media capture early safety-certified design wins as those codecs mature.
insights.locator: It also plans to apply the same functional-safety framework

insights.claim: The article's bottom-line thesis is that as machine perception assumes greater responsibility inside vehicles, proven safety engineering is becoming as commercially important as codec performance, turning video codec IP from a multimedia building block into a dependable component of the automotive safety architecture.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: This signals a broader shift in automotive semiconductor IP markets where certified trust, not just technical performance, becomes a key axis of competitive differentiation as autonomy increases.
insights.quote: The importance of WAVE6331X FuSa lies in trust.
